title: SLC’s Sports City Project Challenged by Stakeholder
byline: A leading and century old cricket club in Sri Lanka, Colts Cricket Club, has challenged Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) to prove the authenticity and transparency of the so-called Jaffna Sports City project in Mandathivu. In a letter fired to the Secretary of SLC, Colts Cricket Club president Nishantha Ranatunga and secretary retired Major General Shiran Abeysekera have asked that the Jaffna Sports City project be clarified to all its member clubs and st

title: 436 post-intern medical officers receive appointments
byline: The Health and Mass Media Ministry has announced the appointment of 436 post-internship medical officers to strengthen healthcare services across the island.

title: Market surges on ceasefire optimism, records one of highest gains in CSE history
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange witnessed a powerful rebound, with both indices posting significant gains in a strongly bullish session. The ASPI surged by over 980 points within the first 10 minutes of trading, reflecting a sharp turnaround in investor sentiment. Although the index moderated thereafter, it maintained a strong upward trajectory, holding gains within the 800–900 point range throughout the session.

title: Iran could open Strait of Hormuz in a controlled way ahead of meeting with US, senior Iranian official says
byline: Iran could open the Strait of ​Hormuz in a limited ‌and controlled way on Thursday or Friday ahead of ​a meeting between ​U.S. and Iranian officials in ⁠Pakistan, a senior Iranian ​official, involved in the ​talks, told Reuters on Wednesday.

title: Trump threatens tariffs of 50% on countries ‘supplying military weapons to Iran’
byline: The U.S. will impose tariffs of 50% on “any and all” goods imported to the country from any nation “supplying military weapons to Iran”, President Donald Trump said on Wednesday.

title: Ministers accumulating social capital while people hit with economic burden: Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa today alleged that Ministers of the government are accumulating social capital while the people are battered with unbearable economic burden.

title: Reduce fuel prices immediately: Sajith tells government
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa today urged the government to immediately reduce fuel prices which were increased due to the Middle East war as a two-week ceasefire has been declared now.

title: Zelenskiy, welcoming Iran de-escalation, says Ukraine ready for ceasefire with Russia
byline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Wednesday he ​welcomed the ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, adding ‌that Kyiv was ready to ’’respond in kind’’ if Moscow ceased strikes.

title: Iranian Oil Refining Company confirms attack on Lavan refinery, Shana reports
byline: An oil refinery ​on Iran’s Lavan ‌Island was targeted in an ’’enemy attack’’ ​on Wednesday ​without causing casualties, ⁠the National Iranian ​Oil Refining ​and Distribution Company said, according to the ​Oil Ministry’s ​news outlet, Shana.

title: Maharagama visa scam: Woman arrested for Rs.10 million fraud promising overseas jobs
byline: A woman from Maharagama has been arrested over allegations of defrauding more than Rs 10 Million by promising foreign employment opportunities in countries including Albania and Canada, The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment  (SLBFE) said.

title: Iraq reopens airspace and all airports following weeks-long closure
byline: In a major step toward normalizing national operations, the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority (ICAA) officially announced the reopening of the country’s airspace and all commercial airports effective immediately.

title: Sri Lanka records nearly 15 million local malware attacks in 2025: Kaspersky
byline: Sri Lanka recorded 14,960,244 local malware incidents in 2025, with 37.4% of users affected by threats spread through removable media such as USB drives, CDs and DVDs, according to the latest Kaspersky Security Bulletin. The country ranks 48th globally for local threat exposure.

title: Greece to ban social media for under-15s from 2027
byline: Greece ‌will ban access ​to ⁠social media for ‌children under ‌the ‌age ⁠of ⁠15 from ​January ‌1, 2027, Prime Minister Kyriakos ‌Mitsotakis said ​on Wednesday, ⁠citing rising anxiety, ‌sleep problems and the ‌addictive ​design of online platforms.

title: Afternoon showers expected in several provinces tomorrow
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at a few places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and North-Western provinces, as well as in Galle, Matara, Kandy, Nuwara Eliya and Mannar districts after 2.00 p.m. tomorrow (April 9), the Meteorology Department said.

title: Council of Arab Ambassadors in Sri Lanka calls on President AKD
byline: A meeting between the Council of Arab Ambassadors accredited to Sri Lanka and President Anura Kumara Dissanayake was held this morning (08) at the Presidential Secretariat.

title: Kuwait Airways to launch Colombo operations from April 15
byline: Kuwait Airways, the national carrier of the State of Kuwait, will commence flight operations to Colombo from April 15, enhancing air connectivity between Kuwait and Sri Lanka.

title: Unlicensed Ayurvedic cream manufacturing plant raided in Matale
byline: Authorities have conducted a raid on an Ayurvedic cream manufacturing facility in Matale following an investigation by the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA).

title: Sri Lanka icon eager to continue ahead of T20WC 2026
byline: Skipper Chamari Athapaththu has given an update on her future to head coach Jamie Siddons.

title: MP Archchuna publishes his pay slip on Social Media
byline: Independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna has published his pay slip on social media, becoming the second MP to do so after MP Jagath Vithana did the same a few months ago.

title: LAUGFS Gas releases 30,000 cylinders daily to meet festive demand
byline: LAUGFS Gas PLC has ramped up its island-wide distribution, releasing approximately 30,000 LPG cylinders daily following the resumption of filling operations at its Hambantota (HBT) and Mabima plants.

title: India orders major airports to cut some charges by 25%, in relief to airlines
byline: India’s airport tariff regulator has ordered major airports to cut landing and parking charges by 25% for three months for domestic flights, offering relief to the country’s airlines that ‌are ⁠under financial ⁠pressure due to the Iran war.

title: MP Ajith Perera forgives Justice Minister
byline: MP Ajith P. Perera told Parliament today that he is ready to forgive Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara for his behaviour in the House the other day.

title: Hezbollah pauses attacks under US-Iran ceasefire
byline: Lebanon’s Hezbollah halted fire ​on northern Israel and on Israeli troops in Lebanon in ‌the early hours of Wednesday as part of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire announced earlier, three Lebanese sources close to the group told Reuters.

title: SriLankan Airlines warns of escalating scam targeting passengers
byline: SriLankan Airlines has alerted the public to a serious rise in scam activities targeting passengers and potential customers through impersonation of airline staff.

title: 12-hour water cut in Mattegoda and surrounding areas
byline: A 12-hour water cut has been scheduled for Mattegoda and several adjoining areas tomorrow (09) due to reduced water supply caused by prevailing dry weather conditions, the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) said.

title: Public consultation begins on proposed Education Council in Sri Lanka
byline: Public consultation has commenced on the report of the committee appointed to submit recommendations for the establishment of an Education Council in Sri Lanka, the Education Ministry announced.

title: Israel issues new evacuation order for Tyre in southern Lebanon, saying it will strike
byline: Israel’s military issued ​repeated urgent warnings ‌to residents of the ​city of ​Tyre on Wednesday ⁠to evacuate ​their homes ​immediately and move north of the ​Zahrani River, ​saying it will ‌strike ⁠the area.

title: Liquor outlets to remain closed on New Year holidays
byline: All liquor shops across the country will remain closed on April 13 and 14 in line with the Sinhala and Hindu New Year period, Excise Commissioner General M.B.N.A. Pemaratne has announced.

title: Dr. Sulakshana Jayawardena appointed acting Chairman of BOI
byline: Dr. Sulakshana Jayawardena has been appointed as the Acting Chairman of the Board of Investment (BOI) of Sri Lanka, the institution announced.

title: Registrar General’s Dept. launches “1930” hotline, new call centre, website
byline: The Registrar General’s Department marked its 161st anniversary with the launch of a dedicated “1930” hotline, a modern call center, and an upgraded official website aimed at improving public service delivery.

title: Banquet and catering charges increased by 15% amid economic pressures
byline: The All Island Banquet Owners and Caterers Association (AIBOCA) has announced that it will increase the prices of food and related services by 15% from April 8, citing rising costs in the face of the ongoing global economic situation.

title: Trump says Lebanon not included in US-Iran ceasefire amid Israeli assault
byline: President Donald Trump has claimed that Lebanon was not included in the ceasefire between the United States and Iran, contradicting the assertion of Pakistan, which mediated the truce.

title: Israel launches 100 air strikes in 10 minutes across Lebanon
byline: Israel carried out an unprecedented wave of attacks across Lebanon, saying it launched 100 air strikes in a span of 10 minutes. Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett reports from the scene of a strike in Beirut.

title: GMOA calls 48-hour island-wide strike over appointment dispute
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has announced a 48-hour island-wide strike set to commence at 8:00 a.m. tomorrow (April 9), citing a dispute with the Health Ministry over post-internship appointments.

title: Iran may quit US ceasefire if Israel continues attacks in Lebanon: Iranian media
byline: Iran will withdraw from a ceasefire agreement with the US if Israel continues to violate it through attacks on Lebanon, an informed source told Iran’s semi-official Tasnim News Agency on Wednesday.

title: Iran halts tanker traffic at Strait of Hormuz after Israeli strikes on Lebanon
byline: Oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has been halted following Israeli attacks on Lebanon, Iran’s Fars News Agency reported on Wednesday.
